doctrine.002: 18 guiding principles and an integrated intervention model
doctrine.003: A State's capacity depends largely on the solidity, coordination, continuity and performance of its institutions.
doctrine.007: Leaders come and go. Institutions must remain able to function.
doctrine.010: Establish the facts before proposing a solution.
doctrine.016: Look for the structural drivers of dysfunction.
doctrine.019: Look for what has been successfully tried elsewhere.
doctrine.022: No foreign model is ever reproduced automatically.
doctrine.028: Texts, procedures, staff, tools, training — everything ready before launch.
doctrine.031: Support concrete implementation, not just recommend it.
doctrine.034: Every intervention has a baseline and documented results.
doctrine.037: Recognize, analyze, correct, retest if necessary.
doctrine.040: Make the institution self-reliant, not create a dependency.
doctrine.045: Digital technology in service of the institution
doctrine.046: Improve the process before digitizing it.
doctrine.049: Separation of duties, traceability, control, transparency.
doctrine.052: Serve the State independently of successive governments.
doctrine.055: A partner may fund the study; it cannot buy its conclusion.
doctrine.058: Decisions of public authority belong to Haiti's own authorities.
doctrine.073: CAPRI does not measure its success by the number of activities carried out, but by the new, lasting capacity left within the institution after its intervention.

tdr.commun_texte: CAPRI's Board of Directors is the collegial body responsible for strategic direction, governance, institutional oversight and safeguarding the organization's interests. Its members carry out their duties solely in the interest of CAPRI, in accordance with its mission, its bylaws, its internal rules, its internal policies and the decisions duly adopted by the Board. Every director is bound in particular by the following principles: collegiality, integrity, confidentiality, diligence, accountability, prevention of conflicts of interest, traceability of decisions and proper use of CAPRI's resources. The Board's functions must remain distinct from day-to-day operational management: the Board directs, authorizes, oversees and controls; the executive team administers and implements.

extra.text: In exercising her oversight duties, the Officer must be able to raise her observations directly with the Board, even when they concern the President, the Vice-President, another director, or an executive officer. She may not be instructed to conceal, alter or suppress a substantial finding within her mandate.
extra.title: Functional independence

extra.text: She exercises an oversight and advisory function, not an autonomous disciplinary one. When an irregularity is found, she documents the facts, formulates her recommendations, and refers the matter to the competent body in accordance with CAPRI's procedures.
extra.title: Important limit

president.limites_intro: The President does not substitute for the Board. Except with express delegation or as provided by internal rules, the President may not:
president.mission: Provide institutional leadership for the Board of Directors, ensure it functions properly, and see that its decisions effectively advance CAPRI's mission and strategic direction.
president.redevabilite: The President is accountable to the Board of Directors collectively.

periodically organizes the evaluation of the Board's functioning

extra.text: No important Board decision should rest solely on informal communications. The Secretary General ensures that institutional decisions are documented, dated, filed and retrievable.
extra.title: Principle of traceability

reseau_experts.fonctionnement: Associate experts may be mobilized for missions, studies, training, analyses, projects, evaluations, or specialized advice.

extra.title: Status
extra.text: Associate experts do not automatically become CAPRI employees, directors, or decision-makers.

reseau_experts.redevabilite: According to the mandate entrusted to them.

cellules_mission.positionnement: Temporary structures set up to carry out a specific CAPRI mission.
cellules_mission.mission: Quickly bring together the skills needed to carry out a defined intervention within a set timeframe.
composition: a CAPRI institutional point of contact
cellules_mission.fonctionnement: Each task force operates under a mandate specifying: purpose, objectives, composition, lead, timeline, resources, deliverables, reporting line, reporting frequency, and closure conditions. Deliverables are expressly defined in that mandate.

extra.title: Duration
extra.text: A mission task force is not a permanent structure. It ends once its mission is completed, unless expressly extended.

cellules_mission.redevabilite: To the structure that entrusted it with its mandate.

values.002: The principles that guide our action
values.005: Honesty, impartiality and respect for responsibilities. No partisan consideration compromises the quality of our interventions.
values.008: Every intervention is prepared, carried out, documented and evaluated to high standards of competence and rigor.
values.011: Optimal use of resources for concrete, lasting results.
values.014: Effectiveness is measured by the observable changes produced within the institution supported, not by the number of activities carried out.
values.017: CAPRI honors its commitments and encourages clarity in responsibilities, timelines and expected results.
values.020: Systems, procedures and skills able to outlast changes in leadership.
values.023: Solutions tailored to each institution's context rather than uniform models imposed from outside.
values.026: Enabling teams to acquire the skills needed to keep improving on their own.
